paper_metadata.title: Tailoring deformation mechanisms in polycrystalline CoNi-base superalloys for enhanced high temperature strength

evidence.quote: here, the importance of additionally tailoring the active deformation mechanisms is shown by correlating the strain-rate dependent high temperature strength of two slightly different polycrystalline CoNi-base superalloys with their underlying defect structures
The two superalloys, PHESA1 (34.8Co-35.0Ni-7.5Al-5.0W-1.0Ti-1.0Ta-12.0Cr-0.4Si-0.1Hf-0.08B at.%)
The alloys were arc-melted using raw materials with a purity of at least 99.9%.
Afterwards, plastic deformation was induced via cold-rolling up to a thickness reduction of 40%.
the alloys were subsequently recrystallized at 1075 C for 4 h in air followed by water quenching
Subsequently, a two-step heat treatment consisting of 900 C for 4 h and 750 C for 16 h, whereby each step was followed by air cooling

correlating the strain-rate dependent high temperature strength of two slightly different polycrystalline CoNi-base superalloys with their underlying defect structures
In this work, we investigated the strain-rate dependency of two complex, polycrystalline CoNi-base superalloys over four orders of magnitude using constant strain-rate and creep experiments.
The alloys were arc-melted using raw materials with a purity of at least 99.9%.
